draft.title: Impacts of consuming goods
card: Consuming goods means buying and using them. Almost everything we consume ends up as waste at some point.
Waste comes from packaging, such as plastic wrap and boxes. It also comes from goods thrown away after use, such as old clothes and electronics.
Most waste in Australia goes to landfill, a large site where rubbish is buried. Some waste, especially plastic, can be blown or washed into rivers and the ocean.
The more goods people buy and throw away, the more waste there is. Waste can harm land, water and wildlife.
draft.remember: Buying and using goods creates waste, and waste ends up in landfill or the ocean.

a.q: Which of these is an impact of consuming goods?
opts: Old phones are thrown away and become waste
A factory clears bush to make space for a plant
A mine uses large amounts of water to make metal
A farm uses energy to run its machines
a.why: Throwing away old phones is waste created after goods are bought and used. The other three happen when goods are made, not when people consume them.
a.clue: Think about what happens after a person buys and uses something.

b.q: Sam buys a new pair of jeans each month and throws the old pair out. Where is the old pair most likely to end up?
opts: In landfill, where waste is buried
In a power station, where it is made into energy
In a farm paddock, where it feeds soil
In a shop, where it is sold again
b.why: Clothes that are thrown out usually go to landfill, where waste is buried. The other options are not where most thrown-out clothes end up, because they are not recycled or reused when simply put in the bin.
b.clue: Where does most rubbish put in a household bin go?

a.best: Old phones are thrown away and become waste

b.best: In landfill, where waste is buried

problems.detail: "Most waste in Australia goes to landfill" is not accurate for total waste. The National Waste Report shows over half of all Australian waste is recovered or recycled, about 60–63%. The line could say "Much of the waste from households" or "Waste that is not recycled goes to landfill".

The remember line says waste "ends up in landfill or the ocean", as if all waste goes to one or the other. The card says most goes to landfill and some "can" be washed into the ocean. It could say "much of it ends up in landfill, and some can reach the ocean".

check.summary: Both questions are sound. The card's claim that most Australian waste goes to landfill is out of line with national data, since over half is recovered, and the remember line overstates where waste ends up compared with the card.
